fullPassage: If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again. And yet, when they grew up, they might still listen to that music and play old games, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again.

(A) I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away.

(B) This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up.

(C) And yet, when they grew up, they might still listen to that music and play old games, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why?

det.korean: 어린 시절 형성된 핵심 기억이 성인이 된 후의 취향과 그리움을 결정한다는 글쓴이의 가설 전개 순서
det.analysis:
① (A) - (B) - (C)
→ (A)는 'I hypothesize'로 시작하는 가설인데, 이는 Why?라는 질문에 대한 답이어야 함. 도입문 다음에 질문 없이 바로 가설이 나오면 흐름이 끊김

② (B) - (A) - (C)
→ (B)의 'This is nothing groundbreaking'은 앞서 제시된 가설을 가리키는 지시어인데, 가설이 아직 나오지 않은 도입문 뒤에 바로 오면 This가 가리킬 대상이 없음

③ (C) - (A) - (B) ← 정답
→ 도입문: 어린 시절 들었던 것은 커서 다시 안 듣는다 → (C): 그런데 커서도 그 시절 음악을 여전히 좋아할 수도 있다, Why?(왜 그럴까?) → (A): I hypothesize로 그 질문에 대한 답 제시(어린 시절 핵심 기억) → (B): This is nothing groundbreaking(이 가설)으로 자연스럽게 연결, 다른 사람들도 이미 같은 말을 했다는 근거로 이어짐

④ (A) - (C) - (B)
→ (A)의 가설이 Why?라는 질문 없이 도입문 직후 등장하면 질문-답 구조가 성립하지 않음. (C)의 Why?가 뒤에 와도 이미 답이 먼저 나와 어색함
det.tip: 지시어(This, these)가 가리키는 대상이 앞에 분명히 있어야 순서가 맞다. (B)의 'This is nothing groundbreaking'은 직전에 가설이 제시되어야 자연스럽다.

det.korean: 주어 they + 조동사 would + 동사 never listen + to that old thing + again.
det.analysis:
먼저 주어와 조동사를 잡아요: they would(그들은 ~할 것이다)가 주어+조동사예요.

그 다음 동사: never listen(절대 듣지 않을 것이다) to that old thing(그 오래된 것을) again(다시는).

그래서 'they would never listen to that old thing again'(9단어)이 완성돼요. never의 위치(조동사 뒤, 동사 앞)에 주의하세요.
det.tip: they + would + never + 동사원형 + to + 명사 + again

questions.wa: they would never listen to that old thing again
accept: they would never listen to that old thing again

questions.passage: If you had a ten-year-old listen to some bandstand from the fifties, or even a mainstream rap video from the eighties or nineties, then showed them the best of what was being offered today, they'd never listen to that old thing again. And yet, when they grew up, __________, and might even prefer them to whatever newer and greater thing came out in their twenties and thirties. Why? I hypothesize that our tastes and values, especially when it pertains to entertainment, have to do with the core memories we form as children, the stuff that wows us, that we've never seen before, that takes our breath away. These memories serve as the foundational bedrock for our understanding of the world and our nostalgia for the 'old days'. This is nothing groundbreaking. There's plenty of others who have said this first and backed it up. It only makes sense that the people we idolize - athletes, musicians, movie stars - still hold our attention and appreciation as we grow old, and that the next wave can't hold up through our more experienced, more cynical, and less forgiving eyes. The same sense of wonder that inspires us as children, when we are so full of hope and possibility, is the one we ignore and put down as we grow older and become more focused on routine and responsibilities. The only difference is timing.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

"그들은 여전히 그 음악을 듣고 오래된 게임을 할지도 모른다."

[조건] (1) and, games, listen, might, music, old, play, still, that, they, to 를 모두 사용
       (2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 주어 they + 조동사 might + still listen to that music + and + play old games (병렬구조).
det.analysis:
먼저 주어와 조동사: they might(그들은 ~할지도 모른다)로 시작해요.

그 다음 두 동작을 and로 병렬 연결: still listen to that music(여전히 그 음악을 듣고) and play old games(오래된 게임을 한다).

그래서 'they might still listen to that music and play old games'(11단어)가 완성돼요. might 뒤에 listen과 play 둘 다 동사원형으로 병렬되는 점에 주의하세요.
det.tip: might + still + 동사원형1 + and + 동사원형2 (병렬구조)

det.analysis:

동사 wow(놀라움을 주다)를 3인칭 단수 현재형으로 바꾸면 wows가 돼요.

그래서 wow를 wows로 써요.
det.tip: wow(동사원형) → wows(3인칭 단수): 놀라움을 주다
